title: Residue comparison for relative integral closure
statement: Let $V$ be a valuation ring [def-trf-valuation-ring] with fraction field $K$, let $\mathfrak p\subset V$ be a nonzero prime, and put $T=V\setminus\mathfrak p$. Let $A$ be a commutative $V$-algebra which is torsion-free as a $V$-module, viewed inside $A_K=A\otimes_VK$. Assume that $A_T=T^{-1}A$ is integrally closed in $A_K$: every element of $A_K$ integral over $A_T$ belongs to $A_T$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. Let $B$ be the integral closure of $A$ in $A_K$. Then $B\subseteq A_T$ and, as ideals in $A_T$, $\mathfrak pA=\mathfrak pB=\mathfrak pA_T$. The induced maps $A/\mathfrak pA\to B/\mathfrak pB\to A_T/\mathfrak pA_T$ are injective, and $B/\mathfrak pB$ is exactly the integral closure of $A/\mathfrak pA$ in $A_T/\mathfrak pA_T$. This statement imposes no finite-height, finite-type or separably closed hypothesis, and includes the zero algebra.

e0$, and the fraction-field characterization of [def-trf-valuation-ring] gives $q/t\in V$ or $t/q\in V$. The latter would imply $t=q(t/q)\in\mathfrak p$, a contradiction, so $q/t\in V$. Since $t(q/t)=q\in\mathfrak p$ and $t
otin\mathfrak p$, primality puts $q/t$ in $\mathfrak p$. Thus division by any $t\in T$ preserves $\mathfrak p$.

proof.text: View $A_T$ as the subring $\{a/t:a\in A,\ t\in T\}$ of $A_K$: each $t\in T$ is nonzero and invertible in $K$, and $A\hookrightarrow A_K$ is part of the hypothesis. Every element of $\mathfrak pA_T$ is a finite sum $\sum_i q_i(a_i/t_i)$ with $q_i\in\mathfrak p$, $a_i\in A$, $t_i\in T$. Step 1 rewrites it as $\sum_i(q_i/t_i)a_i\in\mathfrak pA$. The reverse inclusion is immediate. Hence $\mathfrak pA_T=\mathfrak pA$ as subsets of $A_T$; in particular $\mathfrak pA$ is an ideal of $A_T$.

source.place: Theorem 3.5.5, Step 4, printed pp. 23–24, after replacing the algebra to make its T-localization relatively integrally closed; primary PDF read online, archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: By [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure], $A\subseteq B$ and every $b\in B$ satisfies a monic polynomial over $A$. Regard its coefficients in $A_T$; the same equation makes $b$ integral over $A_T$. The assumed relative integral closedness gives $b\in A_T$. Therefore $A\subseteq B\subseteq A_T$, and $\mathfrak pA\subseteq\mathfrak pB\subseteq\mathfrak pA_T=\mathfrak pA$. All three sets are equal, and by step 2 they are ideals in $A_T$.

source.place: Theorem 3.5.5, Step 4, printed pp. 23–24, after replacing the algebra to make its T-localization relatively integrally closed; primary PDF read online, archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Put $I=\mathfrak pA=\mathfrak pB=\mathfrak pA_T$. Restricting the quotient map $A_T\to A_T/I$ to $A$ and $B$ has kernels $A\cap I=I$ and $B\cap I=I$, since $I\subseteq A\subseteq B$. Thus the induced maps $A/I\to B/I\to A_T/I$ are injective. These are exactly the two induced maps in the statement.

source.place: Theorem 3.5.5, Step 4, printed pp. 23–24, after replacing the algebra to make its T-localization relatively integrally closed; primary PDF read online, archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: For $b\in B$, reduce its monic equation over $A$ modulo $I$. Its residue $\bar b\in A_T/I$ is a root of the resulting monic polynomial over $A/I$. The definition [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure] therefore puts the embedded ring $B/I$ inside the integral closure of $A/I$ in $A_T/I$.

source.place: Theorem 3.5.5, Step 4, printed pp. 23–24, after replacing the algebra to make its T-localization relatively integrally closed; primary PDF read online, archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Conversely let $\bar z\in A_T/I$ be integral over $A/I$, and lift it to $z\in A_T$. Lift the finitely many coefficients of a monic equation for $\bar z$ to $A$, obtaining a monic $P(X)\in A[X]$ of degree $n\geq1$ with $P(z)\in I$. By step 2, $e=P(z)\in\mathfrak pA\subseteq A$. The polynomial $P(X)-e$ is still monic of degree $n$ and vanishes at $z$ in $A_T\subseteq A_K$. Hence $z\in B$ by [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure], so $\bar z\in B/I$. This proves the reverse inclusion. The argument also holds in the zero algebra; it uses no height, finite-type, reducedness or separable-closedness assumption.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q66-73314343a (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item and all 6 of its steps in full. It has no new nodes. Cited nodes: def-trf-valuation-ring (Mathlib leaf, element-or-inverse dichotomy) and def-weil-pbc-integral-closure (Mathlib leaf: a monic equation of degree n>=1, and the integral closure is a subring containing R); each says what its steps take from it. The statement is true and unchanged. Step 1: for any nonzero prime p of V, q/t stays in p for every t in T, by the dichotomy and primality, with q=0 handled. Step 2: pA_T=pA inside A_K, using torsion-freeness for the embeddings. Step 3: B is inside A_T by the relative-closedness hypothesis; then pA=pB=pA_T follows by squeezing. Step 4: the two maps are injective because I is contained in A, which is contained in B. Step 5: reducing B's monic equations mod I puts B/I inside the integral closure. Step 6 (the converse): lift z and a monic P with n>=1; then e=P(z) lies in pA, which is inside A, so P-e is monic over A and kills z, giving z in B. All six steps are genuinely elementary. Small cases checked: A=0, p maximal (A_T=A), A=K, A=V (giving pV_p=p and V/p integrally closed in its fraction field), and a non-reduced torsion-free A. The degree-0 problem when A_T/I=0 is avoided because the definition requires n>=1. Parent check: lem-trf-valuation-reduced-fibre-normalization steps 7-8 use exactly these hypotheses (A' flat, so torsion-free; A'_T=B_T relatively closed) and exactly these conclusions. The item cites only definitions and Mathlib leaves, so there is no off-route use and no tool_uses entry is needed.
